system_overview: This specification models the lifecycle of a voucher as defined in RFC 3506 (Requirements and Design for Voucher Trading System). A voucher is a digital representation of the right to claim goods or services. The specification captures the state transitions a voucher undergoes from creation through to final disposition (redemption or cancellation).
actors_and_components: The system manages a set of vouchers. Each voucher is an independent entity that progresses through its lifecycle. There are no explicit participant roles in this module; it captures only the voucher state machine itself, abstracting away the parties involved in transactions.
state_variables: The system tracks two pieces of state per voucher: (1) the voucher's current status, which can be phantom (not yet issued), valid (issued and active), redeemed (used to claim goods/services), or cancelled (voided), and (2) the lifecycle machine state, which tracks whether the voucher's lifecycle process is in its initial phase, working phase, or completed.
initial_state: All vouchers begin in the phantom status (not yet issued) with their lifecycle machines in the initial phase.
actions: Four operations can be performed on a voucher: (1) Issue: transitions a phantom voucher to valid status and moves the lifecycle to the working phase; this is a one-way transition that cannot be reversed. (2) Transfer: can only occur when a voucher is valid; it represents changing the voucher's holder but does not alter the voucher's status or lifecycle state. (3) Redeem: transitions a valid voucher in the working phase to redeemed status and completes the lifecycle. (4) Cancel: transitions a valid voucher in the working phase to cancelled status and completes the lifecycle.
safety_properties: A type correctness invariant ensures voucher statuses and lifecycle states remain in their expected domains. A consistency invariant ensures that the voucher status and lifecycle state are always compatible: a completed lifecycle must correspond to either redeemed or cancelled status, an initial lifecycle must correspond to phantom status, and a working lifecycle must correspond to valid status.
model_bounds: The set of vouchers is provided as a constant parameter. The model-checking configuration uses three vouchers. Deadlock checking is disabled.
additional_assumptions: The specification does not include fairness assumptions. The transfer operation is a no-op in terms of voucher state (it leaves both the status and lifecycle unchanged), capturing the fact that ownership transfer does not affect the voucher's lifecycle position.
